insight.obstacle: A quantitative lower bound is known for a source set A, while the desired qualitative conclusion concerns a target set B. The proof only establishes A ⊆ B after a finite threshold, so pointwise inclusion cannot be used globally without accounting for the exceptional prefix.
insight.strategy: Reduce the target conclusion to positive linear growth of its initial counting function. Establish that for all n ≥ K, membership in A implies membership in B. The counting lemma gives count_A(N) ≤ count_B(N) + K, because at most K natural indices can lie in the exceptional prefix. If count_A(N) ≥ cN eventually for fixed c > 0, choose N large enough that K ≤ cN/2; then count_B(N) ≥ (c/2)N. A separate lemma converts this positive linear lower bound into positive lower asymptotic density. The prime-gap example composes an eventual analytic inequality that gives set inclusion with this finite-prefix density-transport argument.
preconditions: The count function measures the relevant finite prefix consistently for both sets.
There is a finite natural threshold K after which A-membership implies B-membership.
The source set has an eventually valid lower bound count_A(N) ≥ c*N with a fixed real c > 0.
The exceptional prefix has cardinality at most K under the counting convention; index offsets must be checked if the domain/counting interval changes.
The target density notion is known to follow from a positive linear lower bound; a different density definition may require a different bridge lemma.

transformation.before_state: For source set A, count_A(N) ≥ c*N eventually; for target set B, A ⊆ B is known only for indices at least K. The target's positive lower density is not yet established.
transformation.after_state: Finite-prefix accounting yields count_A(N) ≤ count_B(N)+K. For sufficiently large N the constant K is absorbed into half the linear term, so count_B(N) ≥ (c/2)*N; positive lower asymptotic density follows under the target density's declared bridge lemma.
transformation.expected_obligation_change: Split one qualitative density goal into (1) eventual source-to-target inclusion, (2) a finite-exception counting inequality, (3) absorption of a fixed additive constant into a positive linear lower bound, and (4) the explicit linear-count-to-density bridge.

evidence.supports: The target set inclusion is proved eventually by importing an asymptotic prime-growth inequality rather than assuming a pointwise bound for every index.
The high-level proof uses the eventual-inclusion counting bridge, composing it with the positive-linear-count-to-density result.
The local counting contract explicitly bounds the cost of all exceptions by an additive constant K.
The proof selects a threshold where both the source lower bound applies and the finite exceptional prefix is at most half the linear term.

failure_boundaries: If inclusion only holds on a positive-density subset rather than after a finite threshold, the additive-K argument is not sufficient.
If the source lower-bound coefficient varies with N or tends to zero, the fixed c/2 conclusion does not follow without a uniform positive lower bound.
If infinitely many exceptions are possible, their count must be bounded separately; it cannot be replaced by a finite constant K.
If the counting function uses a different interval or counts zero differently, the exceptional-prefix bound and off-by-one details must be re-established.
A positive linear lower count is stronger than some notions of positive density and may not be the right bridge for arbitrary density variants.
